introduction.situation: Engineering knowledge covers a very wide range of artefacts, from materials to vehicles, power plants and communication networks.
introduction.complication: Published schemes slice the same artefacts by library class, industry list or sector, so the same kind of system appears under many headings.
introduction.question: How is everything in engineering divided by the kind of system designed?
introduction.answer: Engineering is divided by the kind of system the engineer designs: materials and the making of things, structures, machines and vehicles, energy and process systems, and electrical, information and control systems.

field_check.governing_thought: Engineering is divided by the kind of system the engineer designs: materials and the making of things, structures, machines and vehicles, energy and process systems, and electrical, information and control systems.
key_line: Materials and manufacturing systems are designed to make artefacts: material classes, nanostructures, fabrication and production processes.
Structures, machines and vehicles are designed systems whose behaviour is set by force and motion, from aircraft and ships to mechanisms and precision devices.
Energy, fluid and process systems are designed to convert energy or move and transform matter, as in power plants, heat systems, chemical and environmental processes and resource extraction.
Electrical, information and control systems are designed to carry charge, signals and decisions, from circuits and electromagnetics to communications, sensing, robotics and control.
